issue_context.title: Python Tokenizer batch_encode_plus doesn't pad input if asked to do so.
issue_context.body:
```python
input_p = tokenizer_p.batch_encode_plus(
    ["This is a simple input 1", "This is a simple input 2"], 
    max_length=15, 
    pad_to_max_length=True
)
```

Output is not padded

review_comments: (nittiest ever) same as torch.Tensor (upper case?) I assume?

torch.tensor is a factory method which will dispatch creating the actual torch.Tensor   (torch.cuda.DoubleTensor, torch.FloatTensor, etc.) to right type of tensor (float, double, long, byte, bool, etc.) on the right device (device=...) and with the current named tensor parameters / alignment in memory
so we stopped calling encode plus?

also cant you call get_input_ids inside the loop, since it takes a tuple?
and then append without ever splitting first and second ids?

We stopped calling `encode_plus`, which does the following -> 

- Gets strings and converts them to ids *or* gets tokens and converts them to ids *or* gets ids and does nothing with them
- Passes the resulting ids to the `prepare_for_model` method.

`batch_encode_plus` does the same thing, just with an array instead. I changed from calling `encode_plus` to `prepare_for_model` as I need to know the sequence that, once encoded, has the maximum length in that batch as well as that length. This will be used when setting `pad_to_max_length=True`, without a `max_length`, so that it pads the smaller sequences up to the longer sequence's length (useful for creating tensors out of that batch). 

I'm not sure I understand your second comment, though. Do you mean call `get_input_ids` inside the if statement?

Tap me, I can explain first comment.

Re padding: does https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/nn.html#torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_sequence help? `torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_sequence(sequences, batch_first=False, padding_value=0)`

Tap me if you want to discuss the second comment!
Agree that we could probably use pad_sequence if it makes the code simpler (I use it in `run_language_modeling`)
